title: Taidekasarmin muutos ja peruskorjaus, kokonaisurakoitsijan hankinta
description: Taidekasarmin muutos ja peruskorjaus, kokonaisurakoitsijan hankinta Rakennus on valmistunut vuonna 1915, ja se kuuluu Hyrylän kasarmialueen toiseen rakennuskauteen. Kyseessä on yksikerroksinen, massiivitiilirakenteinen rakennus, jossa on ullakko. Rakennuksen omistaa Tuusulan kunta ja se on asemakaavassa suojeltu kulttuurihistoriallisesti ja aluekokonaisuuden kannalta arvokkaana kohteena (sr-24). Rakennus sijaitsee pohjavesialueella. Hanke kattaa rakennuksen peruskorjauksen sekä käyttötarkoituksen muutoksen ravintolaksi. Lisäksi naapuritontille rakennetaan uusi, noin 45 m²:n huoltorakennus, johon tulee ravintolan jätetila. Huoltorakennus toteutetaan poikkeamispäätöksen perusteella ja sen tieltä puretaan nykyinen jätekatos. Huoltoliikenne järjestetään Esikunnanpolun kautta. Kunta tekee urakka-alueen ulkopuolisen varsinaisen katualueen työt. Tilaaja on aiemmin purkanut rakennuksen alapohjan betonirakenteet sekä suurimman osan yläpohjan ei-kantavista rakenteista. Peruskorjauksessa tehdään uudet alapohjarakenteet. Lisäksi sokkeli mantteloidaan teräsbetonilla, kantaviin tiiliseiniin injektoidaan kapillaarikatko ja ensimmäisen kerroksen kattoon asennetaan teräksiset jäykistys- ja vahvistusrakenteet. Osa sisäpuolisista rappauksista poistetaan, ja tiilipinnat puhdistetaan. Julkisivu ja ikkunat kunnostetaan. Ravintolarakennukseen tehdään lisäksi kaksi uutta poistumistieovea, esteetön sisäänkäynti portaineen ja luiskineen, terassi, huoltotaso ja lastauslaituri portaineen ja luiskineen sekä ullakolle johtava kierreporras. Sisätiloihin tehdään ravintolatoiminnan edellyttämät muutokset, kuten valmistuskeittiö ja kylmiöt. Ullakko otetaan osittain käyttöön IV-konehuoneina. Vesikatolle asennetaan uudet IV-konehuoneiden piiput, vesikattovarusteet sekä uudet savunpoisto- ja kattoluukut. Käyttötarkoituksen muutos edellyttää taloteknisten järjestelmien kattavaa uusimista. Rakennustöissä on otettava huomioon haitta-ainekartoitus, kunto- ja rakennetutkimukset sekä museoviranomaisen lausunnot. Ravintolarakennus ja huoltorakennus toteutetaan P1-puhtausluokan mukaisesti. Tarkemmat tekniset ratkaisut on esitetty suunnittelualakohtaisissa työselostuksissa ja erikoissuunnitelmissa. Urakka-alue on asemapiirustuksen mukainen, ja siihen kuuluu myös huoltoliikenne- ja puistoaluetta. Tavoitteena on, että käyttäjä pääsee kalustamaan rakennusta ravintolakäyttöä varten loppuvuodesta 2027 (tarkempi ajankohta tarkentuu myöhemmin).,

Bestandteil der Ausschreibung ist die Lieferung und Montage von: - 24 Deckenlaufschiene mit quer über Patientenplatz verfahrbarer Schiene mit Infusionshalter - 2 Patientenliftersystem, U/B-Raum / Umbettschleuse als 1-Bett-Schwerlastzimmer - 53 Patientenlifter für 1-Bett-Standardzimmer (Allgemeinpflege) - 2 Patientenliftersystem über WC hinwegführend, 1-Bett-Schwerlastzimmer (Allgemeinpflege) - 45 Patientenliftersystem mit Infusionsdeckenschiene, 1-Bett-Standardzimmer (Intensivpflege) - 2 Patientenliftersystem mit Infusionsdeckenschiene inkl. Infusionsstange, 1-Bett-Schwerlastzimmer (Intensivpflege) - 1 Patientenliftersystem mit Infusionsdeckenschiene inkl. Infusionsstange, 2-Bett-Schwerlastzimmer (Intensivpflege) - 2 Patientenliftersystem über CT / Parkposition hinwegführend (CT/CT Notfall) - 20 Patientenlifter, fahrbar Die Lieferung und Montage der Bestandteile soll nach dem folgenden Prioritäten-Schema getrennt ablaufen: Montage Unterkonstruktionen, Montage Deckenlifter, Lieferung Zubehör unmittelbar vor Inbetriebnahme (Diebstahlprävention). Die Einstellung von Anschlägen im Drehbereich ist mit den Nutzern/Vertretern durchzuführen. 1 Haupt- und 1 Nachbesserungstermin sind mit dem Angebotspreis abgegolten, wobei die Teilleistungen gemäß Terminplan gestaffelt einzutakten und mit der örtlichen Bauleitung/Fachbauleitung abzustimmen sind. Die gesetzliche Verjährungsfrist der Gewährleistungsansprüche beginnt mit der Abnahme der Leistung. Der Tag der Abnahme (komplette Montage inklusive Mängelbeseitigungen) ist der Gewährleistungsbeginn. Folgende Leistungen sind neben den gerätebezogenen Leistungen anzubieten und zu kalkulieren: - Bei der Kollisionsprüfung durch den koordinierenden Architekten (4Bund) ist durch den Auftragnehmer (AN) mitzuwirken. Die Montagepläne sind bei Erfordernis anzupassen. - Für Organisationsbesprechungen - auch teil- und abschnittsweise - hat der AN einen mit der Anlage in allen Teilen technisch und betrieblich vertrauten, sachkundigen Mitarbeiter beizustellen. - Weitere Leitungen gemäß den zusätzlichen technischen Vorbemerkungen der Medizintechnik Eignungskriterien gemäß allgemeinen und besonderen Vertragsbedingungen, Punkt 1.10 / Punkt 2.10 Für die Lieferungen und Montagen der Geräte sind folgende Termine maßgebend: Möglicher Beginn Einbau: 04.10.2027 Spätester Abschluss Montagen: 29.03.2029 (Innenausbau + Technik gem. Generalablaufplan_V5) Unter Berücksichtigung des Starttermins ist ein Montageterminplan vorzulegen und ggf. an Vorgaben des Architekten (4Bund) anzupassen. Die jeweils für die Einbringung und Montage benötigten Zeiten sind pro Gerätetyp zu hinterlegen.

title: Detaljprosjektering av VA-anlegg Vennerød–Gravdal
description: Bakgrunn Sandefjord kommune skal knytte sammen VA-nettet mellom Andebu og Stokke. Prosjektet er delt i flere etapper. Etappe 2, som inkluderer pumpestasjonene Vennerød og Fossnes samt ledningen mellom dem, er under detaljprosjektering. COWI er ansvarlig prosjekterende for denne etappen, som skal ferdigstilles ved årsskiftet 2026/2027. Etappe 3 omfatter sammenkoblingen mellom Vennerød og Gravdal. Oppdraget gjelder vurdering og valg av deltrasé samt komplett detaljprosjektering av VA-anlegget og nødvendig geoteknisk detaljprosjektering, slik at kommunen får et komplett grunnlag for utlysning og gjennomføring av entreprisen. Beskrivelse av oppdraget For beskrivelse av oppdraget vises det til vedlegg Oppdragsbeskrivelse og øvrige vedlegg til konkurransen.

title: SWAG Cancer Alliance Lung Cancer Screening Programme
description: Bristol NHS Foundation Trust (BFT), as host organisation for the Somerset, Wiltshire, Avon and Gloucestershire (SWAG) Cancer Alliance, is seeking to appoint a provider to deliver a fully managed Lung Cancer Screening Programme across the Somerset, Wiltshire, Avon and Gloucestershire (SWAG) Cancer Alliance area. The procurement is being managed by Bristol and Weston NHS Purchasing Consortium (BWPC) on behalf of the Trust. The service will identify and engage eligible populations, deliver lung cancer screening services, provide low-dose CT (LDCT) scanning services, and ensure effective management of participant pathways in support of the early detection and diagnosis of lung cancer. The provider will be required to deliver a high-quality, accessible and equitable service that maximises uptake, reduces health inequalities, and complies with all relevant national standards and programme requirements. The contract term is 36 months, with the option to extend for up to two further periods of 12 months each, giving a maximum total contract duration of 60 months. Additional information is contained within the Invitation to Tender documentation available through SAP Ariba.

title: Request for Information: Flexoelectric Future
description: The Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA) Multi X Office (MXO) seeks information to inform possible future research on flexoelectric materials. The Department of War (DoW) requires sensing and transduction technologies that operate under size, weight, power, communications, and environmental constraints. The intended scope of this RFI is foundational materials, interfaces, metrology, design rules, and device elements that may encode or discriminate local mechanical state through strain-gradient-driven electromechanical response.

title: PWA-T3, T5, T6 (sélectif) Appel d'offres pour les travaux électriques, CFC 232 Installations basse tension
description:
L'infrastructure de l'aéroport de Zurich fait l'objet d'un processus de rénovation progressif. Au cours des

15 dernières années, différentes parties de l'infrastructure centrale de l'aéroport ont été entièrement rénovées et agrandies : le Dock B a été entièrement réaménagé, le terminal 2 a fait l'objet d'une rénovation complète et d'un agrandissement, et entre les terminaux 1 et 2, le nouveau bâtiment de contrôle de sécurité, doté d'un accès centralisé à l'Airside Center, a été construit. Actuellement, le centre central de tri des bagages situé au nord du terminal 1 est en cours d’agrandissement et le système de tri des bagages à l’échelle de l’aéroport est en cours de remplacement et de modernisation.


Dans un deuxième temps, les éléments vieillissants de l'infrastructure centrale de l'aéroport

doivent être remplacés : le quai A a été mis en service en 1985 en même temps que la tour de contrôle et est resté, dans sa structure, pratiquement inchangé jusqu'à aujourd'hui. En termes de fonctionnalité, de durabilité et de qualité, le quai A ne répond plus aux exigences actuelles. À la suite d’une analyse approfondie, il a été décidé de remplacer le quai A existant par un nouveau bâtiment situé au nord du bâtiment actuel.


La reconstruction du Dock A, la nouvelle tour de contrôle et la rénovation complète de l'aire de trafic du Dock A, ainsi que toutes les autres adaptations, extensions et transformations de l'infrastructure centrale de l'aéroport, constituent les travaux de construction les plus importants des 15 à 20 prochaines années. Dans le cadre de cette réalisation par étapes, il faut veiller à ce que l’exploitation puisse se poursuivre normalement et que les nouveaux bâtiments permettent de répondre aux futures exigences fonctionnelles.


Le projet PWA.T « Mise à nu du périmètre Wurzel A » est divisé en trois sous-projets (T3, T5 et T6) et comprend la mise en œuvre d’adaptations des réseaux et installations existants. Ceux-ci se trouvent à l’intérieur et à l’extérieur du périmètre de démolition du quai Wurzel A. Les travaux doivent être réalisés en vue de la phase de démantèlement et des phases suivantes du projet principal côté piste. La réalisation des prestations en question débutera dès 2027 et se déroulera par étapes ; conformément au calendrier indicatif du projet (chapitre IV, point 1.1), l’essentiel des travaux se concentrera sur les années 2027 à 2029. Les étapes ultérieures liées au projet principal côté piste pourront suivre, après une interruption prolongée, jusqu’en 2033 environ. Ces dates tardives sont données à titre indicatif uniquement ; elles correspondent à l’état actuel de la planification et sont susceptibles d’évoluer au fur et à mesure de l’avancement du projet. Le périmètre de démolition de la base du quai A abrite des éléments essentiels des installations techniques assurant l’alimentation de la tour de contrôle, de la base du quai A, du quai A, de l’Airside Center et du hall de contrôle des passeports.

title: 13043.10 / 201-01 Spezialtiefbau, Instandsetzung & Erweiterung Betriebsgebäude Seepolizei und Schifffahrtskontrolle Oberrieden
description:
BKP 201-01 Travaux spéciaux de terrassement et d'excavation


Situation initiale

Le canton de Zurich réalise, sur le site d’Oberrieden, la rénovation complète ainsi que l’extension du bâtiment d’exploitation existant de la police lacustre et du contrôle de la navigation.


Pendant la durée des travaux, les activités de police sont transférées dans des installations provisoires déjà réalisées. Le présent appel d’offres concerne les travaux d’excavation et de terrassement du projet principal, à l’exclusion des installations provisoires.


Les travaux d’excavation et de terrassement sont attribués comme lot indépendant (BKP 201-01) et doivent être coordonnés avec les travaux spéciaux de génie civil (BKP 170-01), les travaux de gros œuvre (BKP 211-01) ainsi qu’avec les autres corps de métier.


Vue d’ensemble du projet

Le projet comprend la rénovation du site existant ainsi que son extension. Les prestations de ce lot comprennent principalement :

  • Décapage et stockage intermédiaire de la terre végétale et du sous-sol
  • Excavation de la fouille, approfondissements, mise à niveau du fond de fouille et stabilisation des talus
  • Fourniture de matériaux, remblayages et stabilisation du sous-sol
  • Transports ainsi que valorisation et élimination des matériaux excavés


Le site est situé sur la Seestrasse à Oberrieden (ZH), directement en bordure du lac de Zurich.


Le terrain est constitué de remblais artificiels reposant sur des dépôts lacustres meubles ; seule la roche de molasse sous-jacente présente une capacité portante suffisante. Le niveau de la nappe phréatique correspond au niveau du lac et se situe au-dessus du fond de la fouille.


La parcelle figure au cadastre des sites pollués (KbS). La gestion des matériaux pollués sera effectuée conformément aux prescriptions du spécialiste en sites contaminés.

title: Switzerland – Electrical installation work – PWA-T3, T5, T6 (Selektiv) Ausschreibung Elektro, BKP 232 Niederspannungsinstallationen
description: Die Infrastruktur des Flughafens Zürich unterliegt einem schrittweisen Erneuerungsprozess. In den letzten 15 Jahren sind verschiedene Teile der zentralen Flughafeninfrastruktur umfassend saniert und erweitert worden: Das Dock B wurde komplett umgebaut, der Terminal 2 totalsaniert und erweitert, und zwischen den Terminal 1 und 2 wurde das neue Sicherheitskontrollgebäude mit zentralisiertem Zugang in das Airside Center erstellt. Derzeit werden die zentrale Gepäcksortieranlage nördlich des Terminal 1 erweitert und das flughafenweite Gepäcksortiersystem abgelöst und erneuert. In einem nächsten Schritt müssen die in die Jahre gekommenen Teile der zentralen Flughafen- Infrastruktur ersetzt werden: Das Dock A wurde zusammen mit dem Tower 1985 in Betrieb genommen und blieb in seiner Struktur bis heute weitgehend unverändert. Bezüglich Funktionalität, Nachhaltigkeit und Qualität kann das Dock A die heutigen Anforderungen nicht mehr erfüllen. Aufgrund einer umfassenden Analyse wurde entschieden, das bestehende Dock A durch einen Neubau nördlich des heutigen Gebäudes zu ersetzen. Der Ersatzneubau für das Dock A, der neue Tower und das umfassend sanierte Vorfeld zum Dock A mit allen weiteren Anpassungen, Erweiterungen und Umbauten der zentralen Flughafeninfrastruktur sind die sichtbar wichtigsten baulichen Massnahmen der nächsten 15 bis 20 Jahre. Bei der etappenweisen Realisierung muss gewährleistet werden, dass der Betrieb normal weitergeführt werden kann und mit den neu erstellten Gebäuden die künftigen funktionalen Anforderungen erfüllt werden können. Das Projekt PWA.T «Perimeterfreilegung Wurzel A» ist in drei Teilprojekte (T3, T5 und T6) unterteil und beinhaltet die Umsetzung von Anpassungen an bestehenden Medien und Anlagen. Diese befinden sich im und auch ausserhalb des Abbruchsperimeters der Wurzel Dock A. Die Arbeiten sind für den Bauzustand des Rückbaus und für die weiteren Phasen des Hauptprojekts Luftseite zu realisieren. Die Ausführung der vorliegenden Leistungen beginnt bereits 2027 und erfolgt etappiert; der Schwerpunkt liegt gemäss den indikativen Projektterminen (Kapitel IV, Ziffer 1.1) in den Jahren 2027 bis 2029. Nachgelagerte Etappen im Zusammenhang mit dem Hauptprojekt Luftseite können nach einer längeren Unterbrechung bis ca. 2033 folgen. Diese späten Termine dienen lediglich der Orientierung; sie entsprechen dem aktuellen Planungsstand und können sich im weiteren Projektverlauf ändern. Im Abbruchperimeter der Dockwurzel A sind essenzielle Teile der Gebäudetechnik für die Versorgung des Kontroll-Towers, Dockwurzel A, Dock A, Airside Center und der Passkontrollhalle verortet.

Ireland – Railway construction works – TII499 Luas Finglas Main Infrastructure Design and Construction Works
description: Luas Finglas is a 4 km extension of the Luas Green Line, delivering a high-capacity light rail connection between Finglas and Dublin city centre to support sustainable transport and urban development. The scheme will serve communities including Charlestown, Finglas Village, Finglas West, St Helena’s, and the Tolka Valley, and will comprise four new stops at St Helena’s, Finglas Village, St Margaret’s Road, and Charlestown. It also includes a 350-space Park and Ride facility near St Margaret’s Road, as well as interchange opportunities with bus services and with mainline rail services at Broombridge. The Luas Finglas Main Infrastructure Design and Construction Works will be delivered under the NEC4 Engineering and Construction Contract (ECC) Option C (Target Cost with Activity Schedule). The scope of this Contract (TII-499) includes, but is not limited to, the design and construction of the following principal elements: 1. Site clearance and demolitions. 2. Track (trackbed and rails). 3. Luas Stops at St Helena’s, Finglas Village, St Margaret’s Road and Charlestown. 4. Broombridge stabling site works. 5. Park and Ride facilities at St Margaret's Road. 6. Royal canal and rail overbridge at Broombridge. 7. Tolka Valley Park Bridge. 8. Fencing, retaining walls, boundary treatments and accommodation work. 9. Utility services realignment, diversion, replacement, and protection. 10. Road realignments and junction modifications. 11. Pedestrian and cycling facilities including cycle storage structures. 12. Road traffic signalling. 13. Landscape and urban realm upgrades. 14. Overhead Catenary System (OCS). 15. Power and Systems infrastructure. 16. Signalling, controls and other rail systems. 17. Working in live traffic environment on the busiest radial corridors in the greater Dublin area including property and business frontage reconfiguration. 18. Heritage / archaeology mitigation works. 19. Installation of stop furniture. 20. Installation of Validators and Ticket Vending Machines. 21. Other Ancillary works. The successful Contractor will also be responsible for: • Overall systems integration. • Interfacing and co-ordinating with other works packages to facilitate completion of works. • Interfacing and co-ordinating with stakeholders. • Testing and commissioning.

This pre-solicitation is replacing the one numbered 36C25226B0033. Contractor shall provide all design plans, tools, materials, components, labor, quality assurance, and supervision in accordance with construction documents, drawings and specifications to complete the required construction services. The principal components of work include: upgrading the interiors of elevators P-7B, P-8B, P-9B, and freight elevator S-10B in the Ogden Pavilion. Pursuant to Public Law 109-461, this solicitation is set-aside for Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) firms. The North American Industry Classification Code (NAICS) for this procurement is 238290, Other Building Equipment Contractors; size standard $22.0 Million applies. The solicitation will be issued on or about 11/5/2026 with the bid opening scheduled as shown in the solicitation. The bidder is responsible to monitor and download any amendments from Contact Opportunities at https://sam.gov/contracting which may be issued to this solicitation. GENERAL INFORMATION: This RFI is issued solely for information gathering purposes to identify sources that can provide support for the BioWatch program field operations, special events and surge operations, and technology upgrades and integration. In accordance with FAR 15.101(c), RFIs may be used when the Government wants to obtain price, delivery, other market information, and capabilities for planning purposes. Responses to these RFIs are not offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. This RFI shall not be construed as a commitment by the Government for any purpose, nor does it restrict the Government to an ultimate acquisition approach. Respondents are solely responsible for all expenses associated with their RFI response. Respondents will not receive additional information in response to their submittal to the RFI and will not be notified of the resulting market research. INTRODUCTION: DHS�s mission is to safeguard the American people, the homeland, and American values with honor and integrity. In support of this mission, the FEMA works to prevent CBRN attacks against the United States by providing timely, responsive support to operational partners. The CBRN Support Directorate advances this mission through the BioWatch program, the nation�s only civilian program that monitors for aerosol releases of select bioterrorism agents. Since its establishment in 2003, BioWatch has maintained a bioterrorism air monitoring system that operates 24 hours a day, 7 days a week in large metropolitan areas, known as jurisdictions, and partnered with state and local public health communities to prepare for and respond to bioterrorist events. The BioWatch Program�s strategic objectives are to: Monitor for the highest-priority biological agents that could cause catastrophic outcomes. Protect the nation�s most at-risk locations. Maintain technical oversight of operations in close collaboration with state and local public health partners that execute the program. Conduct advanced development and use federal research and development (R&D) to procure and deploy improved detection capabilities at lower cost. Coordinate federal, state, and local public health preparedness activities to develop operational protocols for initiating response activities following the detection of an agent for which the system tests. Strengthen federal, state, and local stakeholder partnerships and improve operational efficiencies. To accomplish these objectives, each BioWatch jurisdiction maintains a static array of air samplers, the filters of which are collected daily by field operators. These filters are then delivered to a state or local operational laboratory where they are analyzed for select biological agents. Jurisdictions may also elect to surge operations by deploying additional units to monitor special events or increasing the collection cycle (e.g., twice a day collections). In addition, each jurisdiction has an advisory committee that coordinates with the BioWatch program on operations and biological event preparedness activities. At the federal level, the BioWatch program includes field, surge, laboratory, and biodefense preparedness operational components. Figure 1 depicts daily sample operations. Figure 1. BioWatch Sample Operational Process PURPOSE OF RFI Currently field operators and field-related tasks are not staffed by contract. The purpose of this RFI is to evaluate and determine the field staffing and support options for the BioWatch program to meet field operations requirements. The performer must enable the BioWatch program to maintain current field operations and continue to provide high quality, reliable, and timely delivery of field samples to the laboratories. In addition, due to its evolving operational needs, the performer must provide the necessary flexibility and adaptability to ensure BioWatch can address changes in sample collections for both planned events and unforeseen incidents, as well as assist with potential technology assessments, field evaluations, integration, and implementation. DESIRED CAPABILITIES FOR BIOWATCH FIELD STAFFING AND SUPPORT CAPABILITY Competent, proficient, and reliable field staffing is essential to ensure the BioWatch program continues to meet established requirements. In addition, the evolving threats and vulnerabilities that are identified at the state and local level require operational flexibility and adaptability that must be able to be supported with field staff capable of performing field operations and chain of custody in accordance with mission needs. A successful candidate staffing performer will provide field personnel to conduct BioWatch daily operations in select metropolitan cities within the United States. Composition and hierarchy of field staff at each location will be made at the discretion of the performer, with recommendations and concurrence from the BioWatch program. The staffing performer shall: Provide a Program Manager for the contract who will serve as the primary point of contact for the BioWatch Program and DHS Contracting Officer. Provide a primary point of contact, or lead, for each jurisdiction who will provide direct oversight of field staff and be responsible for administrative activities such as: Scheduling field staff and scoping collection routes. Maintaining appropriate documentation (e.g., training documentation, required inventories, etc.) Coordinating delivery times with local BioWatch laboratory. Communicating and coordinating with the BioWatch Field Operations team. Participating in relevant program meetings. Upon request, participating in local advisory committee meetings. Responding to requests for information from the BioWatch program. Supporting program audits and other assessments. Provide local office space to include space for equipment and consumable supplies storage. Implement staff recruitment and retention practices to maintain staffing levels over the life of the contract to: Support routine daily operations 7 days a week, 365 days a year and may require working beyond a standard 8-hour day and/or alternate shifts. Support planned and limited notice special events and surge operations (i.e., equipment deployment/demobilization, increased operations tempo, increased collection cycle, expanded array, etc.). Support changes to the static array (i.e., additions/reductions in number of collection sites) or collection routes. Ensure the staffing level in a given jurisdiction does not fall below 75% for longer than 1 month and that overall staffing levels do not fall below 90% per year. Accommodate appropriate and reasonable time off for personnel (i.e., paid time off, etc.) without compromising operations including special events and surge operations. Provide continuity of operations, which may include: Changes in operational tempo caused by limited notice special events. Travel of field staff from one jurisdiction to another for either surge support or to ensure continued steady-state operations. Perform all required operational tasks in accordance with the Field Operations Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) and other program guidance, processes, and protocols, including: Logistics support. Equipment and supplies ordering and inventory maintenance and reporting. Ensure all field staff, including new hires, are appropriately trained in all relevant BioWatch operations procedures, processes, and protocols. title: Unison
description: The Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA) is soliciting innovative proposals for Unison, a program to develop and evaluate collaborative-autonomy approaches that jointly adapt team decision-making and communications during mission execution. Unison will investigate approaches that enable autonomous teams to modify tactics, behaviors, coordination relationships, and information exchange as mission complexity and operational variability increase and communications become constrained and/or degraded (see Section 7, Glossary, for program-specific definitions of terms in italics). The core hypothesis of Unison is that a unified execution-time reasoning approach to action planning and communications planning can improve the effectiveness, scalability, and resilience of collaborative autonomy in dynamic, uncertain, and resource-constrained environments. Unison seeks to preserve mission performance while reducing communication dependence and bounding the reasoning burden imposed on individual agents. Unison frames collaborative autonomy as a multi-agent decision problem in which agents use local observations, mission context, relevance, and mission objectives to select a policy that jointly defines physical actions and communications actions. At each decision point, the team must determine what actions to take, which coordination relationships must be maintained, and what information must be exchanged to preserve the coordination required for mission success. Unison will investigate approaches across teams of tens to hundreds of agents operating in representative collaborative, multi-domain mission scenarios.

Since its establishment in 2003, BioWatch has maintained a bioterrorism air monitoring system that operates 24 hours a day, 7 days a week in large metropolitan areas, known as jurisdictions, and partnered with state and local public health communities to prepare for and respond to bioterrorist events. The BioWatch Program�s strategic objectives are to: Monitor for the highest-priority biological agents that could cause catastrophic outcomes. Protect the nation�s most at-risk locations. Maintain technical oversight of operations in close collaboration with state and local public health partners that execute the program. Conduct advanced development and use federal research and development (R&D) to procure and deploy improved detection capabilities at lower cost. Coordinate federal, state, and local public health preparedness activities to develop operational protocols for initiating response activities following the detection of an agent for which the system tests. Strengthen federal, state, and local stakeholder partnerships and improve operational efficiencies. To accomplish these objectives, each BioWatch jurisdiction maintains a static array of air samplers, the filters of which are collected daily by field operators. These filters are then delivered to a state or local operational laboratory where they are analyzed for select biological agents. Jurisdictions may also elect to surge operations by deploying additional units to monitor special events or increasing the collection cycle (e.g., twice a day collections). In addition, each jurisdiction has an advisory committee that coordinates with the BioWatch program on operations and biological event preparedness activities. At the federal level, the BioWatch program includes field, surge, laboratory, and biodefense preparedness operational components. Figure 1 depicts daily sample operations. Figure 1. The purpose of this RFI is to evaluate and determine the field staffing and support options for the BioWatch program to meet field operations requirements. The performer must enable the BioWatch program to maintain current field operations and continue to provide high quality, reliable, and timely delivery of field samples to the laboratories. In addition, due to its evolving operational needs, the performer must provide the necessary flexibility and adaptability to ensure BioWatch can address changes in sample collections for both planned events and unforeseen incidents, as well as assist with potential technology assessments, field evaluations, integration, and implementation. DESIRED CAPABILITIES FOR BIOWATCH FIELD STAFFING AND SUPPORT CAPABILITY Competent, proficient, and reliable field staffing is essential to ensure the BioWatch program continues to meet established requirements. In addition, the evolving threats and vulnerabilities that are identified at the state and local level require operational flexibility and adaptability that must be able to be supported with field staff capable of performing field operations and chain of custody in accordance with mission needs. A successful candidate staffing performer will provide field personnel to conduct BioWatch daily operations in select metropolitan cities within the United States. Composition and hierarchy of field staff at each location will be made at the discretion of the performer, with recommendations and concurrence from the BioWatch program. The staffing performer shall: Provide a Program Manager for the contract who will serve as the primary point of contact for the BioWatch Program and DHS Contracting Officer. Provide a primary point of contact, or lead, for each jurisdiction who will provide direct oversight of field staff and be responsible for administrative activities such as: Scheduling field staff and scoping collection routes. Maintaining appropriate documentation (e.g., training documentation, required inventories, etc.) Coordinating delivery times with local BioWatch laboratory. Communicating and coordinating with the BioWatch Field Operations team. Participating in relevant program meetings. Upon request, participating in local advisory committee meetings. Responding to requests for information from the BioWatch program. Supporting program audits and other assessments. Provide local office space to include space for equipment and consumable supplies storage. Implement staff recruitment and retention practices to maintain staffing levels over the life of the contract to: Support routine daily operations 7 days a week, 365 days a year and may require working beyond a standard 8-hour day and/or alternate shifts. Support planned and limited notice special events and surge operations (i.e., equipment deployment/demobilization, increased operations tempo, increased collection cycle, expanded array, etc.). Support changes to the static array (i.e., additions/reductions in number of collection sites) or collection routes. Ensure the staffing level in a given jurisdiction does not fall below 75% for longer than 1 month and that overall staffing levels do not fall below 90% per year. Accommodate appropriate and reasonable time off for personnel (i.e., paid time off, etc.) without compromising operations including special events and surge operations. Provide continuity of operations, which may include: Changes in operational tempo caused by limited notice special events. Travel of field staff from one jurisdiction to another for either surge support or to ensure continued steady-state operations. Perform all required operational tasks in accordance with the Field Operations Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) and other program guidance, processes, and protocols, including: Logistics support. Equipment and supplies ordering and inventory maintenance and reporting. Ensure all field staff, including new hires, are appropriately trained in all relevant BioWatch operations procedures, processes, and protocols. Interested parties may respond to one or both elements identified in this RFI. Any resulting award may be made for one or both of the elements and may result in a single or multiple award to one or more vendors. Training Consultation for Program Revision; Development of Interactive eLearning Content. USPTO�s Patent Training Academy is the training program responsible for preparing new hires to be patent examiners. It is designed to give new examiners the skills, knowledge, and confidence they need to begin their careers. In FY 2026, the USPTO hired 963 new examiners. Currently, the training program is delivered over 10-weeks and is comprised of a 125-course curriculum. The program follows a university-style model that uses a mix of large-lectures and small group lab sessions to give examiners opportunity to apply what they have learned. Through a combination of the use of a practice training application, active learning exercises, lecture and dedicated examination time, the goal of the program is to provide patent examiner new-hires the needed competencies to successfully examine in a Technology Center (TC) with guidance from experienced examiners. OBJECTIVE The USPTO seeks a training partner/partners, that can bring innovative approaches, fresh ideas, and creative solutions to help modernize and strengthen the Patent Training Academy�s content and training delivery. The objective of this RFI is to seek capable contractors who could provide the USPTO with Training Consultation for Program Revision, and Development of Interactive eLearning Content. REQUIREMENTS Training Consultation for Program Revision: The USPTO seeks firms with experience in instructional design consultation services to provide innovative, modern, and forward-looking solutions that introduce new ideas, enhance learner engagement, and create a more effective, scalable, and future-ready training experience for patent examiners, to include: Expertise in instructional design and adult learning theories and principles. Experience providing innovative solutions to enhance engagement and learning in large training programs with extensive curriculums, specifically more than 40 courses in a single curriculum. Experience with providing reimagined experiential learning solutions including Super Intelligence (SI) to enhance learning and taking complex, detailed curriculum and transforming the curriculum to provide faster acquisition of job skills and application of content. Experience in incorporating SI solutions into training delivery models. All SI solutions must be approved by USPTO. Ability to work with subject matter experts to elevate learning objectives and ensure content alignment with learning objectives for highly complex legal and examination procedure topics. Ability to work with subject matter experts to review and upgrade course activities for highly complex legal and examination procedure topics. Ability to work with subject matter experts to review and modernize course teaching methodology for highly complex legal and examination procedure topics. Ability to work with subject matter experts to recommend updated assessments of learning objectives and outcomes. Experience in providing consultation services for legal content. Ability to develop training content and related deliverables in fresh, exciting, and engaging ways with a strong emphasis on immersive and technology-enabled experiential learning solutions with a focus on gamification and simulation-based learning . Experience in recommending appropriate scheduling for redesigned training programs. Ability to recommend ideal learning environment and delivery method, to include in-person learning classroom set-up, classroom technology requirements, hybrid learning delivery, and eLearning content at both headquarters and alternate locations. Ability to recommend fresh and innovative experiential learning solutions, and to provide a range of options in response to unique learning concerns. Development of Interactive eLearning Content: The USPTO seeks firms with experience in the development and implementation of cutting-edge, interactive eLearning content that uses innovative instructional design, interactive learning strategies, artificial intelligence-enabled solutions, gamification, adaptive learning, immersive technologies, contemporary and immersive visual design, dynamic visual elements, and cutting-edge ideas for improving learner engagement and knowledge retention, to include: Expertise in the design of eLearning content, using standard eLearning authoring tools such as Articulate Storyline 360, Adobe Captivate, and similar platforms, including SI-enabled development features where appropriate. All training content must be developed in a shareable and editable file format, firms must not recommend proprietary software or learning management system-solutions. Expertise in incorporating instructional design and adult learning theories and principles to eLearning content. Experience in building an adaptive gamification into eLearning content to increase learner motivation, participation, and retention. Experience in designing microlearning content. Ability to leverage SI-informed approaches to support content development, learner personalization, scenario generation, assessment design, adaptive learning environments or other enhancements, as appropriate. Demonstrated experience in developing interactive eLearning that incorporates the following: SI-powered personalization and adaptive learning Immersive technologies (Augmented Reality & Simulations) Blended and hybrid learning that seamlessly incorporates in person training with interactive eLearning elements Gamification using timed activities, branching scenarios, challenges/missions, and other innovative approaches Contemporary and immersive visual design targeted at adult audiences Ability to work with subject matter experts to ensure the design correctly represents legally accurate materials. Tools used must meet FEDRAMP and other USPTO security requirements. Exp

title: Helo Maintenance - Montana USDA WILDLIFE SERVICES
description: Scope This Performance Work Statement (PWS) defines the requirements for inspection, maintenance, repair, and specialized mission equipment installation services for USDA APHIS Wildlife Services rotary wing aircraft that are assigned to the Montana program or are transiently supported by the State Office. The Contractor must provide all management, personnel, facilities, tooling, equipment, technical data, quality control, parts support, and documentation necessary to perform the tasks and deliverables described in this PWS. Purpose The purpose of this PWS is to establish performance-based requirements for maintaining Government-owned rotary-wing aircraft in an airworthy, mission-ready condition. Required services include 100-hour inspections, 300-hour inspections, annual inspections, scheduled and unscheduled maintenance, troubleshooting, repairs, component replacement, avionics or mission equipment installation, field maintenance when aircraft cannot be flown to the Contractor's facility, documentation, and coordination with Government aviation personnel. 2.4 - Contract Type and Term The government is awarding a firm, fixed-price, indefinite delivery, indefinite quantity, commercial services contract. description: Scope This PWS defines the requirements for providing rotary wing flight services, supporting wildlifedamage management operations in Montana, including all tasks, deliverables, and standards required for safe and compliant flight operations. 2.2 - Background The United States Department of Agriculture (USDA), Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service (APHIS), Wildlife Services (WS) Program in Montana require contracted rotary wing flight services to support their wildlife damage management and related operational missions. The Contractor must furnish, operate and maintain fixed wing aircraft in accordance with the specifications. 2.3 - Purpose The purpose of this Performance Work Statement (PWS) is to identify the required tasks and responsibilities of the Contractor providing rotary wing flight services in support of the Montana WS Programs. Contracted flight operations primarily support activities related to wildlife damage management. Additional missions may include disease monitoring, removal of invasive species, and emergency response operations. Flight requirements may fluctuate based on predation levels, operational priorities, and weather conditions; however, the Contractor must remain available to perform services with a minimum of 72 hours notice. title: USARC Yellow Ribbon Program
description: THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE ONLY. The Mission and Installation Contracting Command - Fort Bragg (MICC-FB) has a requirement to procure services for the United States Army Reserve Command (USARC) Yellow Ribbon Program. Be advised that the U.S. Government will not be able to set aside this requirement if two (2) or more small businesses do not respond with information to support the set-aside. We encourage all small business, in all socioeconomic categories to identify their capabilities in meeting the requirement at a fair market price. This notice is issued solely for information and planning purposes � it does not constitute a Request for Quote (RFQ)/Invitation for Bid (IFB)/Request for Proposal (RFP) or a promise to issue an RFQ, IFB or RFP in the future. This notice does not commit the U.S. Government to contract for any supply or service. Further, the U.S. Government is not seeking quotes, bids or proposals at this time and will not accept unsolicited proposals in response to this sources sought notice. The U.S. Government will not pay for any information or administrative costs incurred in response to this notice. Submittals will not be returned to the responder. Not responding to this notice does not preclude participation in any future RFQ or IFB or RFP, if any is issued. If a solicitation is released, it will be synopsized on the Governmentwide Point of Entry. It is the responsibility of potential offerors to monitor the Governmentwide Point of Entry for additional information pertaining to this requirement. In response to this sources sought, please provide: 1. Name of the firm, point of contact, phone number, email address, UEI number, CAGE code, a statement regarding small business status (including small business type(s)/certifications(s) such as SDB, 8(a), HUBZone, SDVOSB, WOSB, etc.) and the corresponding NAICS code. 2. Identify whether your firm is interested in competing for this requirement as a prime contractor or not. Identify subcontracting, joint ventures or teaming arrangement that will be pursued, if any. 3. Information in sufficient detail regarding previous experience (indicate whether as a prime contractor or subcontractor) on similar requirements (include size, scope, complexity, timeframe, government or commercial), pertinent certifications, etc., that will facilitate making a capability determination. 4. Information to help determine if the USARC Yellow Ribbon services is commercially available, including pricing information, basis for the pricing information (e.g., market pricing, catalog pricing), delivery schedules, customary terms and conditions, warranties, etc. 5. Identify how the Army can best structure these contract requirements to facilitate competition by and among small business concerns. 6. Identify any condition or action that may be having the effect of unnecessarily restricting competition with respect to this acquisition. Please contact the MICC Advocate for Competition, Scott Kukes, at scott.d.kukes.civ@mail.mil or 210-466-3015, if you believe that this action is unreasonably restricting competition. Include the subject of the acquisition, this announcement, and the MICC POC information from the SAM.gov. Provide the specific aspects that unreasonably restrict competition and the rationale for such conclusion. 7. Recommendations to improve the approach/specifications/draft PWS to acquiring the identified items/services. Responses to this notice will assist the government in identifying potential sources and determine if a set aside of this solicitation is appropriate and they will help determine if a single award or multiple award is appropriate.

description: THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE ONLY. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSALS. THIS SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE IS PUBLISHED FOR MARKET RESEARCH PURPOSES ONLY. This notice is issued by the Department of the Navy, Naval Sea Systems Command (NAVSEA HQ), on behalf of NAVSEA Facilities (Enterprise Workspace Management). NAVSEA is comprised of Headquarters (HQ) activities located at the Washington Navy Yard (WNY) and technical/industrial field organizations across more than 40 geographically dispersed activities spanning over 34 million gross square feet of facilities and supporting approximately 80,200 personnel. NAVSEA Facilities seeks to identify potential sources interested in and capable of fulfilling the requirements for enterprise workspace management support services to implement, sustain, expand, configure, and improve the ARCHIBUS Workplace Management System (IWMS) / Computer-Aided Facility Management (CAFM) platform. The current baseline utilizes ARCHIBUS version 25.2 (and approved upgrades) hosted across staging, testing, training, and production environments by the Enterprise Digital Capabilities (EDC) team at NSWC Dahlgren, VA. The requirement encompasses NAVSEA HQ, Program Executive Offices (PEOs), and participating field activities, including Naval Warfare Centers (NSWC/NUWC), Naval Shipyards (Norfolk, Pearl Harbor, Portsmouth, Puget Sound), Regional Maintenance Centers (CNRMC, MARMC, SERMC, SWRMC), Supervisors of Shipbuilding (SUPSHIP Bath, Groton, Gulf Coast, Newport News), and related naval commands. (Incumbent Contract Reference: Currently satisfied under SeaPort Task Order N00178-14-D-8048-EH01 by BlueWater Federal Solutions, Inc. Estimated LOE is approximately 240,910 Direct Labor Hours over a 5-year period of performance: one 12-month base year plus four 12-month option years). title: HYDROSPHERE, BIOSPHERE, & GEOPHYSICS (HBG) SUPPORT SERVICES II - FINAL REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL (FRFP)
description: The National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA), Goddard Space Flight Center (GSFC), hereby invites interested parties to review the Final Request for Proposal (FRFP) for the Hydrosphere, Biosphere, and Geophysics (HBG) Support Services II requirement supporting the Earth Sciences Division (ESD) at NASA/GSFC. The principal purpose of this requirement is to provide science research that conceives, develops, and applies space, field-deployed (i.e. airborne and in situ) and laboratory based technologies and observations to address issues of importance to society. These include but are not limited to water resources, land and ocean ecosystems, global and regional sea level change, changes in the Earth�s cryosphere, gravity field, magnetic field, solid Earth, and the terrestrial reference frame. The Statement of Work, Attachment A, describes the scope of the requirement. This contract is for support of a full range of science and research activities across the breadth of the various Laboratories that make up the HBG sub-division: the Cryospheric Sciences, Ocean Ecology, Hydrological Sciences, Biospheric Sciences, and Geodesy and Geophysics Laboratories. This contract is also for support of science, research and computing activities within the Terrestrial Information Systems Laboratory (TISL), also in the ESD. For the purposes of this document and contract the term HBG will be used to encompass all the Laboratories of the HBG sub-division and the TISL. NASA will conduct this acquisition as a small business set-aside. This competitive acquisition was originally contemplated as a Cost-Plus-Fixed-Fee (CPFF), Indefinite-Delivery/Indefinite-Quantity (IDIQ) contract with the ability to issue CPFF task orders. Following further acquisition planning and assessment of the Government's requirements, the contract structure has been modified. The HBG II Draft Request for Proposal (DRFP) posted on April 8, 2025 was issued as an IDIQ CPFF solicitation. As amended, this competitive acquisition will now result in a HYBRID Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) with the ability to issue Cost Plus Fixed Fee (CPFF) AND Firm- Fixed Price (FFP) task orders. The contract will have an effective ordering period of five years from the contract effective date. Interested offerors are encouraged to review the solicitation and all associated attachments for complete details regarding the requirements and proposal submission instructions. Please see the attached cover letter for additional information.

title: Fuels Management Services at Malmstrom Air Force Base, MT and FE Warren Air Force Base, WY
description: Defense Logistics Agency (DLA) Energy is issuing a Request for Proposal (RFP) for fuels operations and management to include bulk storage services, retail service station support, alongside aircraft services, and entire fuels management services at two Government-Owned, Contractor-Operated (GOCO) facilities, Malmstrom Air Force Base (AFB), MT and FE Warren AFB, WY. The Contractor will ensure safe, accurate, and timely handling, quality control, and accountability of all Defense-Wide Working Capital Fund (DWCF)-owned petroleum products under their control. The Contractor will perform required maintenance to ensure facilities, associated systems, vehicles, and equipment remain operational to meet the base mission. The Contractor shall provide sufficient general-purpose vehicles with appropriate capability to meet the contract requirements but not limited to escorting fuel deliveries where required, towing bowsers, transporting personnel, and performing expeditor duties as needed. The Contractor should provide sufficient special purpose vehicles with appropriate capability to meet the contract requirements for aviation and ground product services. The Contractor will comply with environmental protection, safety, and security directives. The Contractor will conduct required training to ensure personnel are fully qualified to perform Performance Work Statements (PWS) tasks. Tasks identified in the PWS are performed by either the Contractor or Agency as specified in Appendix M The Contractor is responsible for staffing, operations, maintenance, safety, security, environmental protection, training, contractor-furnished items, and Contractor Detailed Plans related to the fuel operations at the location. The Contractor shall conduct all necessary fuels operations to support base operations, airshows and special events, deployments, exercises, and contingencies under normal conditions, as well as, during periods of heightened security, inclement weather, or other unique situations. Operations must be safely and efficiently conducted to receive, store, transfer, issue, and account for fuel products with appropriate controls to ensure fuel quality, inventory accuracy, and no environmental impact. The Contractor shall operate and maintain the self-service automated service station facilities, equipment, and systems and ensure sufficient product is available to provide 24 hours a day, seven days a week support of ground fuels. The Contractor shall perform required tasks to ensure fuel is properly accounted for and issued to only authorized users. This procurement will be 100% restricted to Service Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) participation. Firms submitting a proposal under this RFP must be certified as SDVOSB by the Small Business Administration in accordance with FAR 19.1403. The NAICS Code is 493190 (Other Warehouse and Storage). The Government anticipates awarding two firm fixed-price contracts. This requirement will be for a four-year base period (April 1, 2027 to March 31, 2031), a five-year option period (April 1, 2031 to March 31, 2036), and an option to extend the contract for up to six individual months (April 1, 2036 to September 30, 2036). This procurement will be solicited under full and open competition after exclusion of sources. Interested firms may submit proposals for one location or both locations. The solicitation will be published electronically on the SAM website at https://sam.gov/. Interested companies responding to the solicitation will be required to register in the System for Award Management (SAM) and Procurement Integrated Enterprise Environment (PIEE) prior to submitting a proposal. The Date of the Pre-Preproposal conference, in conjunction with the sites visit will be listed in the solicitation. Offerors will be required to submit in writing to the Contract Specialist (via e-mail) the name(s) and email(s) of the individual(s) who plan to attend by 11:00 AM Eastern Time on October 22, 2026.

title: Request for Proposals (RFP) for Fresh Fruit & Vegetable support for DLA Troop Support's DoW Troop and Non-DoW School and Indian Tribal Organization customers located in Dallas, TX
description: The DLA Troop Support intends to solicit a full-line of produce support for DoD (Troop) customers and Non-DoD (USDA School & Indian Tribal Organization) customers located in the Dallas, Texas Zone. This acquisition will be issued on a small business set-aside (100%) basis. A waiver of the Non-Manufacturer rule has not been requested for this acquisition because it is an acquisition for multiple items. In accordance with 13 CFR 121.406(d)(1), if at least 50% of the estimated contract value of an acquisition for multiple items is composed of items that are manufactured by small business concerns, then a waiver of the Non-Manufacturer rule is not required. As such, for this acquisition, it is expected that items comprising at least 50% of the contract value will be manufactured by small business concerns. The contracting officer must be immediately notified if it appears as though this requirement will not be met. The total length of the contract will be five (5) years. It contains one (1) twenty-four (24) month tier, and two (2) eighteen (18) month tiers. Its estimated maximum total contract dollar value is $243,976,437.00. The delivery points require indefinite quantities of Fresh Fruit and Vegetables throughout the term of the contract. A more detailed listing of the delivery sites can be found in the solicitation. All responsible sources may submit proposals that will be considered by DLA Troop Support. The Government will award a contract(s) resulting from this solicitation to the responsible offeror(s) whose offer(s) conforming to the solicitation will be most advantageous to the Government, price and other factors considered. The source selection method for this procurement will be the Lowest Price Technically Acceptable (LPTA) source selection procedures and shall use the following to evaluate offers: 1. Technical Acceptability - A technically acceptable offer is an offer that takes no exceptions to the terms and conditions in the solicitation and complies fully with all submission requirements, including submissions relating to the two subfactors listed below. A proposal that takes exception to solicitation terms and conditions or that fails to comply with all submission requirements may be deemed technically unacceptable and, thus, may be found ineligible, and removed from further consideration for the award. By submitting a proposal with no exceptions, an offeror is confirming it possesses the necessary facilities, equipment, technical skills and capacity to successfully provide all items required by this solicitation. The following sub-factors will be evaluated and must be found acceptable for a proposal to be eligible for award: A. Perishable Agricultural Commodities Act (PACA) License - The offeror shall possess and submit proof of a valid current PACA license. B. USDA Harmonized Good Agricultural Practices (GAP) Plus + Standard Audit with warehouse and food defense addenda and/or USDA Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP) audit - The Contracting Officer will require an offeror to submit a valid USDA Harmonized GAP Plus + Standard audit, including addenda for warehouse and food defense, and/or USDA GMP audit, or an independent third-party certifying company audit report(s) / certificate for each place of performance identified in the offeror's proposal. The audit report(s) must demonstrate a passing score in the following parts: General, Warehouse and Food Defense addenda. In lieu of a USDA Harmonized GAP Plus + Standard and/or USDA GMP audit report / certificate, the offeror may submit an audit report / certificate conducted by a recognized private independent third-party certifying company certifying to an industry recognized food safety standard that exceeds all aspects of the USDA Harmonized GAP Plus + Standard audit and/or USDA GMP report / certificate requirements. Offerors relying on a non-USDA Harmonized GAP Plus + Standard and/or USDA GMP audit report / certificate that do not agree to have a USDA Harmonized GAP Plus + Standard and/or USDA GMP audit report / certificate for each place of performance prior to the start of contract performance will be found technically unacceptable. 2. Pricing - Pricing is required for all items found in the Schedule of Items (for Group 1 and 2 (2a and 2b), if applicable) and for all tiers. Failure to offer pricing for all items and for all tiers may result in a proposal being removed from consideration for award as technically unacceptable. The Government will perform an aggregate price analysis on all items found in the Schedule of Items (for Group 1 and 2 (2a and 2b), if applicable). To determine an offeror's Evaluated Aggregate Price for Group 1, the Weighted Aggregate Distribution Price will be added to the Aggregate Delivered Price. To determine an offeror's Evaluated Aggregate Price Group 2 (2a and 2b), the Weighted Aggregate Distribution Price will be added to the Aggregate Delivered Price for each sub-group 2a and 2b, respectively, to come to a preliminary Evaluated Aggregate Price for each sub-group. Then, the preliminary Evaluated Aggregate price for 2a and 2b will be added together to determine the offeror's Evaluated Aggregate Price for Group 2. Please refer to paragraph (d) below for further details regarding these price components. The award(s) will be made on the basis of the lowest Evaluated Aggregate Price (for each group) of proposals meeting or exceeding the acceptability standards for non-price factors. The Government reserves the right to remove item(s) from the Schedule of Items. Prior to award, the offered prices of the presumptive awardee(s) will be evaluated on an individual line-item basis to determine whether each price is fair and reasonable using analytical techniques deemed appropriate by the Contracting Officer in her/his complete discretion. A. Price Components: 1. Weighted Aggregate Distribution Price: Aggregate Distribution Price is obtained by first multiplying the proposed distribution price for each item in the Schedule of Items by the item's estimated quantity to calculate the total distribution price for each item. Then, the total distribution prices of all items will be added together to determine the total distribution price for tier 1. The total distribution price for each subsequent tier will also be calculated. The total distribution prices for all tiers will be added together to determine the Aggregate Distribution Price. The Aggregate Distribution Price is then multiplied by a weighting factor of 6 to arrive at the Weighted Aggregate Distribution Price. Note: the weighting factor is applied only to the overall Aggregate Distribution Price (not on a line item basis), and is to be used for evaluation purposes only. The Government's use of a weighting factor of 6 for distribution pricing is done in order to more accurately balance the significance of the pricing components and their respective impact on any subsequent contract(s) issued under this solicitation. 2. Aggregate Delivered Price: The Aggregate Delivered Price is obtained by first multiplying the proposed delivered price of each item in the Schedule of Items by the item's estimated quantity to calculate the total delivered price for each item. Then, the total delivered prices of all items will be added together to determine the total delivered price for tier 1. The total delivered price for each subsequent tier will also be calculated. The total delivered prices for all tiers will be added together to determine the Aggregate Delivered Price. 3. Evaluated Aggregate Price: The Evaluated Aggregate Price is obtained by adding the Weighted Aggregate Distribution Price and Aggregate Delivered Price together. 4. For purposes of the Price Proposal Evaluation, Weighted Aggregate Distribution Price and Aggregate Delivered Price are considered equal. This equality is accounted for mathematically by applying a weighting factor of 6 (based on current Government data) to the Aggregate Distribution Price. Option

title: Commercial Bottled Water Supply and Delivery Support � Republic of Peru (SOUTHCOM AOR)
description: Notice Type: Sources Sought / Request for Information (RFI) Title: Commercial Bottled Water Supply and Delivery Support � Republic of Peru (SOUTHCOM AOR) Issuing Agency: Defense Logistics Agency (DLA) Troop Support � Subsistence NAICS Code: 312112 (Bottled Water Manufacturing) PSC Code: 8960 (Beverages, Nonalcoholic) Response Due Date: 04 December 2026 at 1500 EST 1.) Disclaimer & Purpose BLUF: The Defense Logistics Agency (DLA) Troop Support is conducting market research to identify qualified commercial sources capable of manufacturing, bottling, and delivering potable bottled water to U.S. Department of War (DoW) / U.S. Army personnel operating within the Republic of Peru. Per FAR Part 10 (Market Research) and FAR 15.201(e), this notice is issued solely for information and planning purposes; it does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP) or Request for Quote (RFQ), nor does it restrict the Government as to the ultimate acquisition approach. The Government will not reimburse respondents for any costs incurred in responding to this notice. 2.) Scope of Requirement DLA Troop Support anticipates a requirement for recurring commercial delivery of packaged potable water to designated locations within Peru. Requirement Element & Specification / Details Product Types Individual bottled water cases (e.g., 500 mL / 1 Liter bottles) and/or 5-gallon (approx. 18.9�20 Liter) polycarbonate/PET water jugs. Delivery Cadence Multiple scheduled deliveries per week (FOB Destination) to designated U.S. military operating locations in Peru. Packaging & Labeling Commercial-grade, tamper-evident sealed containers compliant with U.S. and Peruvian food safety and potable water standards. Shelf Life Minimum remaining shelf life of 6 months upon delivery. 3.) Mandatory Quality, Sanitary & Contracting Requirements To be eligible for a future contract award, interested vendors and their production facilities must satisfy two critical gates: Gate 1. Sanitary Approval (APHC Audit) Mandatory Requirement: All water bottling/manufacturing plants must be listed in the Directory of Sanitarily Approved Food Establishments for Armed Forces Procurement (per MIL-STD-3006 / AR 40-657). Action / Threshold: If already approved: Provide your plant establishment number. If not currently approved: The production facility must undergo and pass an initial on-site sanitary audit conducted by the U.S. Army Public Health Command (APHC) / Veterinary Services prior to contract award or product delivery. Gate 2. SAM.gov & CAGE / NCAGE Registration Mandatory Requirement: Vendors contracting directly with DLA must possess an active registration in the System for Award Management (SAM.gov), a Unique Entity ID (UEI), and a Commercial and Government Entity (CAGE) or NATO CAGE (NCAGE) code. title: Y1JZ--Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) Design-Build & Construction Multiple Award Task Order Contract (MATOC) National VA Healthcare Construction Program
description: The VA requires multiple indefinite-delivery, indefinite- quantity (IDIQ) Multiple Award Task Order Contract (MATOC) type contracts to provide construction services enterprise wide. The objective of this procurement is to award multiple IDIQ MATOCs for construction services nationwide within specified pools. These pools will meet the VA infrastructure needs for construction, renovation, maintenance, and repair within the 50 United States and its territories. The MATOC will consist of three (3) SDVOSB Pools with a minimum of ten (10) awardees each and one (1) National Unrestricted Pool with a minimum of ten (10) awardees. The SDVOSB Pools will be set-aside for Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Small Business. Please see RFP, attachments, and appendices for further information.

description: Program Acquisition Executive Marine Corps (PAE MC) Program Manager Tactical Communications & Electromagnetic Warfare Systems (PM TCE) is assessing industry�s capability to provide Commercial-Off-The-Shelf (COTS) tactical camera systems, lenses, and accessories under a Hardware-as-a-Service (HaaS) operating lease model. title: Surface Combat Systems Engineering and Integration
description: REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) / SOURCES SOUGHT ANNOUNCEMENT DEPARTMENT OF THE NAVY Program Acquisition Executive Mission Systems (PAE MS) Capability Portfolio Executive Combat Systems & Fires (CPE CS&F) Integrated Combat System (ICS), PMW 630 SECTION 1: GENERAL INFORMATION Document Type: Request for Information (RFI) / Sources Sought Notice Solicitation / Reference Number: N6175027R1201 Contracting Activity: Navy PAE Mission Systems, Washington Navy Yard, DC Program Title: Surface Ship ICS Engineering and Integration North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Code: 541330 � Engineering Services (Military and Aerospace Equipment and Military Weapons) Product Service Code (PSC): AC13 � R&D: Defense Systems: Weapons / R425 � Support - Professional: Engineering/Technical Response Due Date: 04 December 2026, 15:00 EST Classification Level: Primary document UNCLASSIFIED. Classified responses or annexes up to SECRET / NOFORN handled by separate coordination (see Section 7). SECTION 2: STATUTORY DISCLAIMER & SPECIAL NOTICE This RFI is issued solely for information and planning purposes in accordance with FAR 15.101(c). This notice does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP), Invitation for Bid (IFB), or an announcement of a forthcoming solicitation. Issuance of this notice does not obligate the Government to issue a formal solicitation or award a contract. The Government will not pay or reimburse any costs incurred by respondents in preparing, submitting, or demonstrating information in response to this notice. All submissions become Government property and will not be returned. Participation in this RFI is voluntary. Failure to respond will not preclude a vendor from participating in any future competitive acquisition, should one be released. Respondents may submit capability statements addressing any subset or all of the focus areas detailed herein. SECTION 3: BACKGROUND & PROGRAM CONTEXT 3.1 Background & Context Modern surface warfare requires rapid, modular capability delivery across the Navy's surface fleet. The Navy�s ICS program is making this vision a reality through use of virtualization, Kubernetes orchestration, and development of a common suite of mission applications enabling a "build once and deploy across the fleet" methodology for delivery of capability to frigates, destroyers, amphibious ships, aircraft carriers, future manned and unmanned vessels, and future foreign military sales vessels. The ICS program is conducting market research to identify industry partners capable of executing comprehensive systems engineering and software integration for U.S. Navy surface combat systems. This scope is currently being executed under the N00024-23-C-5117 contract awarded to Lockheed Martin Rotary & Mission Systems in September 2023. 3.2 Technical Scope & Baselines The technical scope spans current and next-generation baseline configurations running incremental deliveries of the Integrated Combat System (ICS) software stack (infrastructure services and tactical platform services) and common mission applications. Applicable ship deliveries include the following: ICS-Enabled AEGIS Combat System Baselines 9.C3+ and Baseline 10.1+ running on Mk6 Mod0/1 hardware with IaaS ORDALT or on Mk6 ModX hardware ICS-Enabled Ship Self-Defense System (SSDS) platforms FF(X) 3 and follow DDG 1000 class in line with delivery of the Zumwalt Enterprise Upgrade Solution (ZEUS) Future USN and FMS platforms SECTION 4: TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS & CAPABILITY AREAS SOUGHT The Navy seeks detailed technical capabilities, corporate competencies, and innovative methodologies across eleven (11) functional areas. Vendors may respond to any or all of the following scope areas: Focus Area 1: Programmatic Engineering, Configuration Management & Governance Configuration Management (CM): Formulating, baselining, and executing Configuration Management Plans (CMP), software build/release planning, Configuration Control Boards (CCBs), and tracking and adjudicating Software Change Requests (SWCRs). Programmatic & Systems Planning: Developing, maintaining, and synchronizing project-level Roadmaps, Integrated Master Schedules (IMS), and capability delivery cadences. Focus Area 2: Systems Engineering & Requirements Architecture Technical Baseline Artifacts: Developing, updating, and managing formal engineering artifacts: Systems Engineering Plans (SEP). Software Development Plans (SDP) utilizing modern Agile/DevSecOps frameworks. System / Subsystem Definition Documents (SSDD). System / Subsystem Specifications (SSS). Software Product Specifications (SPS). Interface Requirements Specifications (IRS). Requirements Traceability Verification Matrices (RTVM) maintaining end-to-end bidirectional requirement-to-test traceability. System Safety Plans (SSP) conforming to MIL-STD-882E and naval weapon safety requirements. Requirements Allocation: Decomposing ICS, AEGIS, SSDS, and future combat system Top Level Requirements (TLR) into modular capability building blocks and subsystem specifications across surface ship classes (DDG 51, CG 47, FF(X), DDG 1000, L-Class, CVN, unmanned surface vessels, FMS variants, future platforms). Technical Leadership: Serving as lead technical authorities in Integrated Product Teams (IPTs), Working Groups (WGs), formal milestone reviews (SRR, PDR, CDR), and leading Technical Interchange Meetings (TIMs) to define and allocate interface requirements. Force-Level Mission Thread Analysis: Evaluating complex, distributed kill-chain mission threads, establishing functional allocations, and resolving tactical latency challenges. ICS Re-Architecture & Model-Based Systems Engineering (MBSE): Authoring SysML/UML MBSE models and leading modular product development across the ICS Domain Architecture. Sensor Management. Vehicle Management. Information Management. Training Management. Tactical Decision Management. External Communications Management. Weapon Management. Display Management. Infrastructure Services. Focus Area 3: Fleet Data Analysis, Feasibility Studies & Gap Assessment Conducting engineering feasibility studies, system performance assessments, and trade studies for capability insertion across diverse ship classes and configurations. Extracting, parsing, and analyzing live fleet exercise data, weapon telemetry, and real-world tactical events to identify performance anomalies and drive capability enhancement. Assessing combat system shortfalls, bottlenecks, and operational gaps, and designing/evaluating candidate architectural and software modifications to close these gaps. Focus Area 4: Tactical Software Design, Coding, Testing, and Integration Combat System Design activities including analysis and algorithm development Mission software development, unit testing, and component integration. Cloud-based and Hardware-in-the-Loop (HWIL)-based testing to include element integration, subsystem testing, and system testing System Integration: Engineering and integrating software interfaces for specific sensor, weapon, and C2 programs and capabilities, including but not limited to: Patriot Advanced Capability-3 Missile Segment Enhancement (PAC-3 MSE) The Standard Missile (SM) Family of weapons (including all Air Defense, Ballistic Missile Defense, and Extended Range Active Missile variants) MK-41 VLS-compatible canister-launched weapons (including Evolved SeaSparrow Missile (ESSM), Tomahawk Land Attack Missile (TLAM), and Vertical Launch ASROC (VLA) Rolling Airframe Missile (RAM) Electronic Warfare (EW) systems Phased array and rotating radar systems Evolving to common track management solution across AEGIS and SSDS configurations Containerized payloads Tactical Virtualization Configurations: Designing, provisioning, benchmarking, and troubleshooting virtualized tactical hardware/software configurations and hypervisor-to-bare-metal runtime environments. Focus Area 5: Hardware/Software Tech Stack, Microservices & System-of-Systems Integration Third-Party Software & Micro

The term "contract" encompasses a contract, an order, or a project work order. 3.2.2 OVERHAUL: An overhauled part is one which has been disassembled, cleaned, inspected, repaired as necessary (by replacing or repairing all components which have been found to exceed limits established by the repair/overhaul manual) reassembled and tested in accordance with the approved repair/overhaul manual listed in this SOW and returned to a Ready for Issue (RFI) condition (Refer to contract schedule for items to be overhauled). 3.2.3 REPAIR: A repaired part is one which has been restored to a Ready for Issue(RFI) condition (by replacing or repairing those components found to be defective, broken, damaged or inoperative during the initial evaluation and troubleshooting phase) and tested in accordance with the approved repair/overhaul manual listed in this SOW (Refer to contract schedule for items to be repaired). 3.3 3.0 SCOPE 3.3.1 GENERAL. If the Government disapproves the requested change, the contractor shall replace any delivered items repaired using such unapproved manuals,drawing, specification, repair source or repair facility change. The contractor is not entitled to any equitable adjustment to the contract price or terms based on the Government's disapproval of a requested change to manuals, drawings, specifications, or to a repair source or facility. 3.4.2 References on Drawings and Specifications:For repair and overhaul purposes only. When notifying the Procurement Contracting Officer of the reasons for making substitutions, the type of change shall be indicated by code number in accordance with one of the following statements: Code 1: PART NUMBER CHANGE ONLY - If the Manufacturer's Part Number indicated thereon has changed, but the parts are identical in all respects, supply the item and advise NAVICP-MECH immediately of the new part number.
